rubric_mode_reason: GP-135 MLH family member. Newton-mode enforces the Generative Yield dimension; the Cross-Substrate Invariant Stance dimension further enforces family-level reasoning. See docs/concepts/mlh_family_protocol.md.

secondary_observable_contract.observable: Family-level prediction beyond fitting this substrate's visible values.
secondary_observable_contract.measurement: Use the MLH packet and scoring scripts to evaluate composition class, prime-power rule, coprime composition rule, or a sealed sibling-substrate prediction.
secondary_observable_contract.expected_range: The proposal distinguishes this substrate from at least one sibling and gives an evaluable prediction for a held-out or sealed family member.
secondary_observable_contract.falsifier: The proposal only predicts additional values of this same table, offers a lookup rule, or cannot be evaluated from the exported MLH packet.

enable_dag_steering_reason: GP-135: DAG steering focuses mutator attention on the weakest belief-node each iter. Useful for preventing the mutator from camping on single-substrate fit-refinement at the expense of family-level structural claims.
farther_tail_region_disable_reason: MLH family substrates use visible + holdout only. The family-level generative claim is scored against F6 (sealed holdout substrate), not via per-substrate farther-tail gates.
runner_allowed_imports_reason: Discrete integer substrate; the bounded-discriminator suite may need sympy for primality / factorization / divisor checks when authoring falsification tests.
disable_named_import_gate_reason: GP-135 family: mutator reasoning ABOUT prime structure is unavoidable given py_exec primitives and the family charter. The denylist is a cold-recovery discipline; Path B requires the mutator to describe its composition class. The cross-substrate invariant check replaces the named-import gate as the contamination guard at the family level.
persona: You are a skeptical mathematician investigating an integer-valued function f(n) defined on positive integers. You have been given raw (n, z) pairs. You are also aware (but cannot prove from this substrate alone) that this is ONE MEMBER of a family of related substrates authored under the same protocol. You demand exact integer match AND you demand that the law's structural class be identified and located within a family of siblings. A proposal that fits z(n) without stating how it would differ from a sibling substrate is descriptive (Kepler-class), not generative (Newton-class). You reward proposals that pre-register a prediction about a hypothetical related substrate, because such predictions are the only cheap falsification test available before the principal reveals the sealed holdout.

dimensions.name: Primary Fit Quality
dimensions.description: Does f(n) reproduce the evidence exactly on visible and holdout points? Exact-integer match is required; any residual is a structural defect. This dimension is the floor, not the headline — compare its weight to Cross-Substrate Invariant Stance (30). A proposal that fits this substrate perfectly but offers no family-level stance should not dominate the overall score.

dimensions.name: Structural Derivation
dimensions.description: Does the thesis derive the functional form from specific observed data tuples rather than assuming a family? Every structural claim must cite observations. Named mathematical results (sequences, laws, functions) score 0 on this dimension.

dimensions.name: Parsimony
dimensions.description: Compact structural rule preferred. Lookup tables and ad-hoc piecewise constructions score 0 regardless of fit.

dimensions.name: Generative Yield (Newton-mode)
dimensions.description: Does the proposal name a secondary observable — a distinct, mathematically-orthogonal prediction the mechanism entails beyond reproducing z(n)? Examples: a value for f(1), a functional identity f(a*b) for coprime a,b, a closed-form sum over primes. Scoring: 0/20 if the proposal predicts only z(n); 10/20 if it names an observable without evaluation method; 20/20 with named observable and explicit evaluation. Trivial restatements ('predicts the next value') score 0.

dimensions.name: Mechanism Algorithmic Concreteness
dimensions.description: Hard gate on verbal-vs-algorithmic primitives. Full credit requires naming at least one: a specific sandbox primitive the expression calls; a cited algorithm; a specific numeric threshold with derivation. Class-of-technique labels ('multiplicative reasoning', 'structural arithmetic') without a runnable primitive score 0.

dimensions.name: Cross-Substrate Invariant Stance
dimensions.description: This is an MLH family rubric. The mutator is expected to treat its proposal for this substrate as ONE MEMBER of a family of related substrates. Full credit requires the thesis to state explicitly: (a) which structural class the proposed law belongs to — e.g., completely additive over a multiplicative decomposition, completely multiplicative, count-valued on a decomposition, neither; (b) what observable would distinguish this substrate's law from a sibling substrate in the same class but with a different per-prime weighting; (c) a pre-registered prediction about a hypothetical related substrate (a functional identity or value at a specific composite n that would hold for some siblings and not others). Proposals that treat this substrate as isolated — no family stance, no sibling prediction — score 0 on this dimension regardless of fit quality.

criteria.1_Fit_Quality_Visible: Does f(n) return the exact integer z for every data tuple in evidence.txt?
criteria.2_Structural_Derivation: Does the thesis show explicit intermediate steps citing specific data tuples?
criteria.3_Parsimony: Compact rule preferred; lookup tables score 0.
criteria.4_Generative_Yield: Does the proposal name a calculable, mathematically-orthogonal secondary observable beyond the primary fit?
criteria.5_Mechanism_Algorithmic_Concreteness: Does the mechanism name a specific primitive, algorithm, or numeric threshold, not just a class of technique?
criteria.6_Cross_Substrate_Invariant_Stance: Does the thesis locate this substrate's law within a family of siblings and pre-register a prediction distinguishing it from nearby members?

disable_evidence_fit_gate_reason: GP-135 fix (2026-04-24): MLH is Path B (primitive-assisted) — py_exec exposes factorint/primefactors/etc., so the gate s anti-overfit-via-pre-training purpose does not apply. holdout_hard_gate already enforces exact-match on the holdout; global_evidence_fit was redundant and was firing asymmetrically (NaN from stale-state imports) on substrates where gate_harness reported clean pass. F5 was the visible victim; F1-F4 happened to write expressions that survived both gates by coincidence.
